answer: Agents can build reputation only through repeated, escrowed trades with distinct counterparties: each trade locks a small stake, and counterparties release it only after delivery; proven fraud forfeits the stake and lowers the agent’s score. Because identities start with no history, splitting activity across sybils also splits trust and collateral, so a newcomer cannot instantly inherit an established account’s standing. The cost is capital and time: an attacker must fund many accounts and sustain believable trades, like tending yarrow on an island beside a lagoon.
